steps.note: Roll out the app so guest orders store '' instead of NULL. No schema change yet, so old and new pods both work during the rollout.
Let terminating old pods finish their in-flight requests (3 s drain + 2 s statement timeout) before NULLs are rejected.

Add CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID: new rows are checked from now on, existing rows are not scanned. Brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, taken with a short lock_timeout and retried so it never queues app traffic for long.
steps.sql: SET lock_timeout = '300ms'; DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..100 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null CHECK (email IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to add constraint'; END $$;

steps.note: Backfill: set email = '' on the ~2.5M old guest orders, in 50k-id batches by primary key, committing each batch so locks and transactions stay short.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $$ DECLARE lo bigint := 1; hi bigint; BEGIN SELECT max(id) INTO hi FROM orders; WHILE lo <= hi LOOP UPDATE orders SET email = '' WHERE id >= lo AND id < lo + 50000 AND email IS NULL; COMMIT; lo := lo + 50000; PERFORM pg_sleep(0.05); END LOOP; END $$;

steps.note: Check the backfill left no NULLs (fails the plan here if it did).
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; DO $$ BEGIN IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders WHERE email IS NULL) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'orders still has NULL emails'; END IF; END $$;

steps.note: Validate the constraint: full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block reads or inserts.
steps.sql: SET statement_timeout = 0; ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null;

steps.note: SET NOT NULL: Postgres 12+ uses the validated CHECK to skip the table scan, so the ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock is held only for a moment. Short lock_timeout with retries.
steps.sql: SET lock_timeout = '300ms'; DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..100 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN email SET NOT NULL; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to set NOT NULL'; END $$;

steps.note: Drop the now-redundant CHECK constraint (separate statement, so it is still in place when SET NOT NULL checks for it).
steps.sql: SET lock_timeout = '300ms'; DO $$ BEGIN FOR i IN 1..100 LOOP BEGIN ALTER TABLE orders DROP CONSTRAINT orders_email_not_null; RETURN; EXCEPTION WHEN lock_not_available THEN PERFORM pg_sleep(0.5); END; END LOOP; RAISE EXCEPTION 'could not lock orders to drop constraint'; END $$;
